pricingNotice: Pricing, availability, and model behavior change frequently. Confirm current details in official vendor documentation before choosing a model or making a purchase decision.

openai.text: Still the starting point for normal professional work on OpenAI. Choose Luna for clean high-volume tasks, Terra for repeated production work, Sol High when several sources or tradeoffs appear, and GPT-6 Astra only when Sol Extra High or Sol Pro is not enough.
uses: Writing, planning, reports, and everyday coding
Clear ways to control reasoning depth
Hardest computer-use and quality-first work on Astra

anthropic.text: A practical route for production agents and complex coding. Use Opus 5 at high when quality is the priority, then reserve Fable 5.1 for the rare cases where Opus falls short.
uses: Long coding runs and tool workflows

xai.text: Start with the flagship for general work. Select 4.3 when your context needs exceed the standard window or when a lower price is useful for a large input. Grok 4.7 is not generally available.

google.text: The current Flash workhorse for everyday coding, agents, and multimodal tasks. Keep 3.7 Flash if a workflow is pinned. Upgrade to Pro only when Flash has trouble with the actual logic or synthesis required. Use 3.8 Live for low-latency voice agents.

balanced: A quick route for polished emails, updates, and short rewrites. Step up to Sol Medium when stakeholder dynamics or sensitivity matter.
speed: Use this for repeatable short updates where speed and cost matter most.
quality: Use this when tone, persuasion, or several stakeholders deserve extra judgment.

balanced: A reliable general route for reports, planning, spreadsheets, and everyday professional judgment.
speed: A cost conscious workhorse for repeatable professional workflows.
quality: Choose this when the deliverable needs stronger synthesis and carefully checked reasoning.

balanced: Use this for several sources, constraints, calculations, or tradeoffs.
speed: A fast route for broad research and source gathering before deeper analysis.
quality: Use this for nuanced, ambiguous, or high impact research where checking work is valuable. Move to GPT-6 Astra when computer use or end-to-end professional work is the bottleneck.

balanced: A solid starting point for routine coding, debugging, and practical implementation.
speed: A focused option for interactive coding when efficiency is the primary goal. Gemini 3.8 Flash is the Google equivalent.
quality: A strong route for architecture, large refactors, and demanding tool based coding work. Fable 5.1 or GPT-6 Astra if Opus is visibly falling short.

balanced: Use this for clean extraction, classification, routing, and batch transformations. Luna list pricing is now in the cheap high-volume band.
speed: A fast option for well defined high volume classification and extraction.
quality: Use this when exceptions, business rules, and richer validation enter the workflow.

balanced: A careful starting point for expensive mistakes, difficult ambiguity, and serious technical review.
speed: Maintain a strong reasoning baseline when time is limited, then add targeted review where risk is greatest.
quality: Reserve this for final production reviews, computer-use work, and high value deliverables where Sol Pro is no longer the ceiling.
